title: Affinity scoring and warmup shaping for attention kernel orchestration
creator: Jenna Park
description: Problem: During FlashAttention v3 rollouts we observe intermittent tail-latency regressions and decode jitter on medium->long contexts. Root causes appear to be suboptimal kernel selection when runtime warm state (KV cache, workspace fragmentation, micro-batches) diverges from profiling samples. Goal: Implement an affinity-scoring layer that selects kernel variants based on sequence-length distribution, recent allocation patterns, and a short warmup shaping policy that smooths prefill->decode transitions without increasing steady-state cost. Success metrics: reduce 95th/99th token latency regressions vs v2 baseline to <+5% and eliminate visible quality-of-service jitter on canary traffic. Constraints: no per-request heavyweight profiling, keep extra memory <6% on dedicated nodes, maintain existing rollback hooks.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Jenna Park: Initial triage after runtime-canary-2025-02-12 showed 99p token latency delta +28% on A100-40GB for seq>2048 when using fa3; v2 baseline was stable. Collected profiles (allocations, microbatch sizes, kernel choice history) for 48h. Opened engineering investigation.

2025-02-16 - Marco Li: Reproduced locally with synthetic workload (batch=4, seq=3072). Observed warmup spike during first 6 tokens of decode where kernel chooser switches from tiling-8->tiling-16 mid-request because prefix KV growth crosses a threshold. Hypothesis: threshold hysteresis too narrow; eviction/warmstart scheduling causes workspace fragmentation that leads kernel scorer to flip to a higher-latency kernel.

2025-02-18 - Marco Li: Design decision: implement an affinity scorer that combines (a) recent per-shard sequence-length histogram (last 128 requests), (b) current workspace fragmentation metric, and (c) a short-term warmup score decayed over N tokens. Score maps to kernel bucket (fast-small, fast-large, fallback-stable). Add guardrails: only change kernel at token boundaries of prefill->decode transition, and require score delta > 0.25 to switch during decode to avoid oscillation.

2025-02-19 - Design review (Liam Ortega): Approved approach but requested canary rollback plan and metrics. Added requirement to track kernel-change rate (switches/sec) and correlate with decode jitter. Also requested an experiment to add a transient workspace reservation to avoid fragmentation during critical transitions.

2025-02-20 - Marco Li: Implemented prototype in runtime branch feat/affinity-warmup (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4238). Prototype changes: affinity scorer module, warmup-shaping policy, and two knobs: score_smoothing_window=32 and switch_threshold=0.25. Added unit tests and microbench harness to emulate KV growth patterns.

2025-02-21 - Benchmarks: Using microbench harness on A100-40GB with model: rwin-13b-lm, configs: {batch=4, beam=1}. Baselines: fa2 stable: median token latency 11.2ms, 95p 23.8ms, 99p 36.1ms. fa3 without affinity: median 10.9ms, 95p 31.1ms (+30%), 99p 46.3ms (+28%). fa3 + affinity prototype: median 11.0ms (+0.9% vs fa2), 95p 24.7ms (+3.8%), 99p 37.9ms (+5.0%). These are preliminary but show improvement on tails with minimal steady-state cost.

2025-02-22 - QA (Nina Gomez): Synthetic long-context soak (72h) with canary traffic shape; observed reduced oscillation but two incidents where affinity chose fallback-stable kernel for >120 tokens causing throughput drop on one shard. Root cause: workspace-reservation heuristic failed under cross-shard eviction pressure. Filed follow-up sub-issue ENG-214010 to add shard-transfer-aware reservation and telemetry.

2025-02-24 - Safety & Rollout Plan (Jenna Park): Canary rollout plan: canary-1 = 2% traffic for 6h, observe kernel-switch-rate, 95/99 token latency, and error rate. Canary-2 = 10% for 24h with canary-tagged clients (internal product teams). Rollback criteria: 95p token latency > +10% sustained for 30m or kernel-switch-rate > 0.5/s per shard. Implemented automatic kill-switch in control plane (runtime-operator HTTP endpoint) and dashboard (https://dash.redwood.internal/runtime/affinity-canary).

2025-02-25 - Marco Li: Addressed QA incident by bounding transient reservation per shard to 4% of GPU memory and adding eviction-prioritization to prefer non-cold allocations. Re-ran soak: no repeat incidents in 24h. Updated PR with patch and added e2e regression test that simulates cross-shard eviction. New PR diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4238/files.

2025-02-26 - PM sync (Aisha Rahman): Confirmed metrics to monitor post-rollout (95p/99p token latency, kernel-switch-rate, avg workspace fragmentation, canary error rate). Agreed to ship as opt-in runtime flag (runtime.affinity=on) in runtime-1.20 for initial enterprise customers; default-off for hosted API until canary completes. Set release target runtime-1.20 and tracking ticket for console visibility to breakout kernel choice per request (PM-4082). Next steps: finalize PR, add perf dashboard tiles, and schedule canary on 2025-03-02.
OPEN ACTIONS: finalize unit-level deterministic test for switch hysteresis; add eBPF/allocator hook to measure fragmentation cheaply; coordinate with infra for canary capacity reservation.
